question: Find the area (in cm²) of an equilateral triangle whose sides are 18 cm.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The area of an equilateral triangle can be computed directly using the square of its side length.

Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × a²

Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 18 × 18

Area = 81√3

**∴ The correct answer is 81√3 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the equilateral triangle (a) = 18 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × a²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f54b878a90d10c52c649e52d493a43b8c5ef7a423f12c7c5436417678335338f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × (18)²

⇒ Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 324

⇒ Area = 81√3 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 81√3 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Altitude of an Equilateral Triangle

The height or altitude (h) bisects the base and divides the triangle into two equal right-angled triangles. Formula: h = (√3 ÷ 2) × a.

Inradius of an Equilateral Triangle

The radius (r) of the inscribed circle touches all three sides from the inside. Formula: r = a ÷ (2√3).

Circumradius of an Equilateral Triangle

The radius (R) of the circumscribed circle touches all three outer vertices. Formula: R = a ÷ √3.
